A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–25 are identical; differences are confined to the first page.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-100 experiments, downstream Raptor evaluations in Table 1, ablations in Table 2, and dynamical and intervention analyses, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original training experiments, downstream evaluations, ablations, and dynamical and intervention results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The max-cut partitioning, tied recurrent blocks, teacher-forcing/autoregressive training, depth scaling, and reconstruction losses are unchanged in Sections 2–3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-100, ImageNet, ADE20k, and NYUv2 coverage, with identical classification, segmentation, depth-estimation, and representation-dynamics scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same DINOv2 ViT-S and ViT-B comparators. Figure 3 and Appendix B retain the same random contiguous and non-contiguous partition comparisons.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, frozen-backbone linear probes, metrics, preprocessing, and testing procedures remain identical in Sections 2–4 and Appendices A–D. No runtime measurement protocol is added.

E4.justification: The training-component ablations, stochastic-depth sweep, architecture and overtraining controls, perturbation analyses, and layer-swapping intervention are unchanged, including Figures 13–15 in Appendix F.

E5.justification: Both versions report Raptor results over three differently seeded model runs as mean plus/minus standard deviation. The ten-sample random-partition comparisons and other uncertainty displays are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match. For example, Table 1 retains ImageNet-1k accuracies of 81.2±0.2, 83.0±0.1, and 83.2±0.1 for Raptor with two, three, and four blocks, respectively; the appendix results are identical.

T1.justification: The BRH definition, partitioning derivation, dynamical definitions, and Levin-complexity claims and proof are unchanged, including the runtime-parity assumption in Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract changes 'equivalent computational cost' to 'equivalent runtime,' but v1 already explicitly claims equivalent runtime and the same runtime budget in Section 3. The BRH, accuracy-recovery, and dynamical-interpretability claims retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of recurrent reuse, angular attractors, token specialization, and low-rank dynamics are identical. Section 5 retains the same qualifications about unresolved causal mechanisms and the residual performance gap.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, layer partitions, preprocessing instructions, and the project access link are unchanged. The abstract wording supplies no new timing measurements or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to recurrent architectures, distillation, dynamical systems, and complexity theory are identical. The updated publication-status footer does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract replaces 'computational cost' with 'runtime.' The first-page footer changes from 'Preprint. Under Review.' to an ICLR 2026 acceptance statement, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. No sections or paragraphs are reorganized.

P2.justification: The first page has limited abstract line reflow and updated footer and version-stamp displays. Figures 1–15, Tables 1–4, and the rendered layout of pages 2–25 are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 makes a terminology adjustment consistent with v1's existing runtime discussion and updates publication metadata. The methods, evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, so these first-page edits do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
